questions.q: What does a SOQL parent-to-child query look like structurally?
options: A subquery nested inside the parent query's SELECT list, e.g. SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account
A standard SQL JOIN between two objects
Two separate SELECT statements joined by a semicolon
A WHERE clause containing an IN subquery
questions.explain: Parent-to-child queries nest a full child subquery inside the outer query's SELECT list — there's no JOIN keyword in SOQL.

questions.q: In SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts) FROM Account, why does the inner FROM say 'Contacts' instead of 'Contact'?
options: It's the child relationship name (plural for standard relationships), not the object's API name
It's a typo that Salesforce silently corrects
SOQL requires all object names to be pluralized everywhere
Contacts is an alias the developer must define first
questions.explain: The subquery's FROM uses the relationship name — usually the plural of the object for standard relationships — not the object name itself.

questions.q: What does a custom relationship name always end in, inside a parent-to-child subquery?
options: __rel
_child
questions.explain: __r marks a traversable relationship name; __c is reserved for custom fields and custom objects, not relationship names.

questions.q: In SELECT Name, (SELECT LastName FROM Contacts WHERE Title = 'CEO') FROM Account WHERE BillingState = 'GA', what does the inner WHERE filter?
options: Which Contacts come back within each Account, independent of the outer Account filter
Which Accounts come back overall
Nothing — inner WHERE clauses are ignored in subqueries
It filters both Accounts and Contacts simultaneously as one condition
questions.explain: The inner subquery's WHERE and ORDER BY operate independently on the child records within each parent, separate from the outer query's filter.

questions.q: Why is there no direct T-SQL equivalent to a SOQL parent-to-child query written in a single statement?
options: T-SQL has no syntax for nesting a full child subquery inside a parent's SELECT list that returns a nested result per parent row
T-SQL doesn't support subqueries at all
T-SQL requires every query to use SELECT *
T-SQL and SOQL are actually identical in this respect
questions.explain: T-SQL would normally need a separate child query or a JOIN that flattens rows — SOQL's nested subquery preserving parent/child structure in one query is genuinely distinctive.
